standard-dialogue-warhammer.npc: I've been posted here to guard this chasm.
Not great. There's constant bursts of hot air, demon roars and strange lights coming from inside.
And then there's the cultists. They just climb out like it's normal to be down there. Try to talk to you like it's business as usual.

options.text: How long are you posted here?

steps.player: How long are you posted here?

steps.npc: Indefinitely. We don't know what the cult is up to and we don't want to be caught unprepared.
No. I signed up to to protect Kourend, even if that means standing outside of a demon nest. Besides, it's not like any demons have come out of it yet.
Thanks.

standard-dialogue-scimitar.npc: What do you want? Are you with those cultists?
Good. I've had enough of their games.
They start off polite, but before you know it, they're trying to get you to agree to something.
They're not fooling me though. The next one that crosses me is going to regret it!

steps.player: About the cultists... What sort of things do they ask you to agree to?

steps.npc: Usually they want you to follow them somewhere private. Some of the bolder ones try to get you to join them inside the chasm.
If it were up to me, we'd launch a sortie right now. See how they like it if we come down on our own terms.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about the demons?

steps.npc: You sound like the lieutenant.
I am. If you ask me we should be out fighting lizardmen. That means we need to go on the offensive and wrap this chasm business up.

steps.player: I take it the rest of your squad aren't as keen.

steps.npc: You'd be right. The lieutenant is too cautious and the rest are too timid. The way some of them speak you'd think they had demon families.
If you see any cultists lurking around, let me know.

standard-dialogue-dagger.npc: I might as well be if we're going to continue this performance.
There are no demons coming out of this chasm. If there were, we wouldn't last long.

options.text: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.player: You think the demons would overrun you?

steps.npc: Demons don't die the same way we do. We could hold back a few of them, but not an endless stream.

steps.player: You seem to know a lot about them.

steps.npc: I do, which means I know that guarding the chasm is a pointless endeavour. Not that the lieutenant cares what I think.
Launching an attack into the chasm would also be pointless. That leaves us with only one other option.
No. We should talk to them. Try to reach an understanding.

steps.player: Somehow I don't think negotiating with demons will end well.

steps.npc: If you have a better idea, go ahead.

options.text: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.player: Aren't you a bit too calm about this?

steps.npc: No. If they wanted to, Yama and his demons could overrun this little squad.
The fact they haven't means they're probably not interested in doing so. As a matter of fact, they seem quite polite.
I didn't say that, But there's evidence to suggest that Yama and his cult can be reasoned with.
If Lord Shayzien is interested in diffusing the threat, he should consider trying to reach an agreement with them.

steps.player: I've met Lord Shayzien. He doesn't seem like the type to compromise.

steps.npc: You've met Lord Shiro Shayzien?

steps.player: Yes, I've met the leaders of all of the houses. Even King Artur Hosidius himself.

steps.npc: Interesting. You're quite the worldly fellow. Perhaps King Hosidius would make a more level headed negotiator. Maybe you could talk to him?

steps.player: I imagine he's quite busy at the moment.
